learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the method and knowledge required to describe, understand and design industrial production and storage systems, define their maintenance criteria, and efficiently use project management tools with statistical basics. Learn the structure and operating principle of industrial plants in terms of organization and management of raw material transformation into finished product, reliability of complex systems, role of human resources and industrial automation, production flows and layout, KPI and performance measurements.

Apply acquired knowledge in real design contexts, as well as in multidisciplinary or non-familiar areas, particularly to the industrialization of a production process, starting from a feasibility study, defining the best production structure and management, assessing the possibility of using automated operations to replace manual ones and controlling the process through KPIs.

Understand and critically evaluate the main production systems (forced and not-forced technological processes, production or assembly, manual or automated); analyze existing systems and assess their performances and adequacy, assess the impact of strategic, planning and operational decisions, and measure plant performances.

Acquire specific vocabulary inherent to production plants and communicate the main contents of the course, both written and orally, such as ideas, engineering issues, and related solutions. Communicate knowledge through appropriate tools, solving numerical problems using common industry methods such as tables, diagrams, flow charts, and numerical spreadsheets.
Deepen knowledge of production plants through autonomous consultation of specialized books, scientific or divulgative journals, even outside the topics explained during lectures.

syllabus_topics: Impact of automation on manufacturing and assembly processes
Theory of reliability for the maintenance of production systems
teaching_methods: Seminars by managers of multinational corporations

assessment_methods.method: Written test based on open questions

assessment_rules: Verification of knowledge takes place through a written test based on open questions, lasting 2.5 hours, usually consisting of 11-12 questions. Theoretical demonstrations have a weight of 1.0, plant design and technical drawings 1.5, and exercises 1.8. The final grade is calculated by assigning a mark in the range 0-30 for each question and then performing the weighted average of the individual evaluations, with final ceiling to the next unit. The test is passed if it reaches a score of at least 18 points. "30 cum laude" is given to students who achieve the highest score on each item and use precise vocabulary. The examination will be carried out in presence or online with suitably adapted methods.
